chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no thing greater in reward than the testimony that there is no god except Allah. Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, nothing can equate to Him, and no one shares with Him in the affairs.'

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god except Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the greatest reward mentioned in Shia hadith for a specific act of worship?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes the Shahadah as the pinnacle of reward, grounding its supremacy in the absolute uniqueness (Tawhid) and incomparability of Allah. This narration underscores the Shia theological emphasis that the declaration of monotheism is not merely a verbal affirmation but the foundational act that aligns the believer with the Divine essence, which has no equal or partner in any affair.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Hamza who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is none from a thing of greater Rewards than the testimony that there is no god except Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic. Nothing can equate to Him<sup>azwj</sup> nor can anyone participate with Him<sup>azwj</sup> in the affairs’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from abu Hamza who has said the following: “

I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) saying, ‘There is nothing greater in rewards than testifying to the truth and believing in the meaning of the testimony of belief in Allah: ‘No one deserves to be worshipped except Allah’, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, Who has no equal and no one shares Him in any issue. ’”
